title: The black stone lifted together
hookLine: at thirty-five he settles the tribes' quarrel over the stone with a cloak (sirah)

lines: CLAN BY CLAN, WALL BY WALL.
cards: Before the quarrel, there was a rule about money. The Ka'ba was old and damaged, and the clans of Quraysh agreed to pull it down and build it again.
Ibn Ishaq says one of their elders stood up and told them: put nothing into this House but clean money. Nothing earned from usury, nothing from prostitution, nothing taken unjustly from anyone.
They agreed, and built, clan by clan, wall by wall. Today: al-Amin.

teach.b: A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, from 'Aishah, says the Prophet told her that her people's funds fell short, and so a part of the old House was left outside the new walls.
That's the space behind the low curved wall on one side of the Ka'ba, the Hijr. Pilgrims circle outside it, because it belongs to the House. The Qur'an remembers who raised the House's foundations.
Pickthall's words: "And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House." So the clans were rebuilding, imperfectly, something they believed Ibrahim had begun.
Then came the corner where the Black Stone sits, and every clan wanted the honor of setting it in place. Ibn Ishaq says the quarrel went on for days, and the clans came close to fighting.
They agreed to let the next man through the gate decide. It was the one they called al-Amin, the trustworthy; Ibn Ishaq says he was thirty-five.
He asked for a cloak, laid the stone on it, and had a man from each clan take hold of the edge. They lifted it together, and he set it in the wall with his own hand.
That closes a week in the household: the trustworthy one, Khadijah's caravan, her proposal, their children, Zayd, Ali, and a cloak with room for every hand.
Next comes the mountain, and the revelation.

how: Pilgrims circling the Ka'ba pass outside the curved wall of the Hijr, and touch, kiss or gesture toward the Black Stone, following the Prophet's ﷺ example.

o: the chief who rebuilt the Ka'ba's walls
a judge chosen by lot to settle quarrels
the trustworthy, Quraysh's name for him

games.q: the black stone lifted together — tap the pairs.
p: the rule for rebuilding the House
the part left outside the walls

s: Quraysh used any money they had to rebuild
they agreed on clean money only, Ibn Ishaq says, and it ran short.
the curved wall of the Hijr marks part of the old House
'Aishah's hadith in Bukhari says funds fell short, so it was left outside.
one clan won the honor of lifting the stone
a man from every clan took hold of the cloak, and they lifted it together.

games.q: the clans are ready to fight over who sets the stone, and they've asked you to decide. what do you do?
o: set it yourself, so no clan wins.
put it on a cloak and let every clan lift.
games.why: he spread a cloak, laid the stone in it, and every clan took hold. then he set it in the wall with his own hand.

practice: Think of a disagreement near you, at work, at home, in a group chat, where each side wants the honor or the last word.
Don't pick a winner; picture the cloak instead, and let one small, practical idea come that would let every person take hold of an edge. If you pray, ask for wisdom in it.

wordCard.voice: Al-Amin, the trustworthy. The name Quraysh called him when the clans feared fighting over the Black Stone, and he set it in place so every clan could lift it together. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: everyone a corner. Nobody won the stone, and nobody lost it. Until tomorrow.

sources.q: And when Abraham and Ishmael were raising the foundations of the House
